transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-04
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Rebecca Lin (Redwood AE), Carlos Mendes (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (Nova Edge CTO), Mark Li (Nova Edge Staff ML Engineer), Jorge Alvarez (Nova Edge Platform Eng)

Summary:
- Intro / qualification on Nova Edge's use-case: conversational agents + knowledge base retrieval, mostly customer-facing chat and internal ops tooling.
- Discussed Redwood PLG quickstart (free credits, SDKs, time-to-first-token) and options for Dedicated / Private later.
- Security, SOC 2, VPC, and KMS questions surfaced.
- Agreed next steps: pricing + security pack, trial org with credits, and SE benchmark session.

[00:00] Rebecca: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Rebecca from Redwood, AE on the account, and with me is Carlos who will do a little bit of the tech deep dive.
[00:12] Aisha: Hi, thanks, yeah appreciate it. We're excited to, uh, see what's quick to get running.
[00:18] Carlos: Hi, all — Carlos Mendes, Platform SE. Quick agenda: 1) understand your planned integration and success criteria; 2) show how our PLG quickstart gets you to first token; and 3) talk about hosted vs dedicated vs private for production.
[00:30] Jorge: Sound good. We're mostly interested in quick onboarding then a pilot for usage on our customer chat product.
[00:42] Mark: And we want to validate latency SLOs, cost per 1k tokens, and data retention — because some of it touches PII.

[01:05] Carlos: Totally. Quick question: current infra — are you running models in-house now or using a cloud API?
[01:12] Aisha: Right now we have a homegrown microservice calling a large cloud provider endpoint for chat and a separate vector DB. We want to reduce cost and get more predictable latency. Also curious about on-prem for regulated customers.
[01:28] Rebecca: Good — that fits a lot of teams we talk to. Our PLG flow is self-serve sign-up, you get free credits, and SDK quickstarts to get a token in minutes. For production we offer Dedicated reserved capacity and Private (VPC or on-prem) deployments.

[02:05] Mark: How fast is time-to-first-token? We need something the product team can demo to customers within a day.
[02:12] Carlos: If you follow the quickstart we send, typically under 15 minutes to get a key and run the SDK example. First real inference might be ~5-15 seconds total depending on your network and model choice.
[02:30] Jorge: Are the SDKs language-specific? We use Go + Python.
[02:34] Carlos: We have official Python and Node SDKs; community Go SDK exists and we have sample curl commands. The REST API is simple, so Go teams often do a tiny wrapper in under an hour.

[03:00] Aisha: For the quickstart free credits — how much do you provide and what's the expiration?
[03:06] Rebecca: We typically seed a trial org with $500 in credits valid for 30 days for PLG quickstarts; for larger pilots we'll add more. Carlos will provision for you after the call.

[03:40] Mark: Cool. On the security front — SOC 2 and SSO are musts for us. We also need audit logs and server-side encryption with customer-managed keys (KMS).
[03:51] Carlos: Redwood supports SOC 2 Type II, SSO / SAML, RBAC, and we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for Private deployments. For hosted customers we offer encryption at rest and in transit; for strict KMS requirements we recommend Private or Dedicated with KMS integration.
[04:15] Aisha: Is there an options doc? We need to show security posture to procurement.
[04:20] Rebecca: Yes, I'll share the security pack and SOC 2 report. I'll include a short matrix of features across Hosted / Dedicated / Private.

[05:00] Jorge: On performance — we care about tail latency below 300ms for short chat prompts and p99 under 800ms for longer prompts if possible. Is that feasible with hosted?
[05:12] Carlos: For small models / optimized routes it's realistic. Hosted can hit low latencies, but latency is variable depending on model and region. Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and fixed GPU pools which helps p99. Also batching and KV cache can reduce average cost but may increase tail latency if configured agressively.
[05:40] Mark: We heard quantization can push cost lower but degrade quality — any guidance?
[05:45] Carlos: Yeah, quantization profiles trade off a bit of quality. We provide recommended quantization levels per model and workload; Redwood Optimize gives suggestions based on your sample prompts. For customer-facing chat you may want less aggressive quantization.

[06:25] Aisha: What's the onboarding for Dedicated? We might start hosted and then move to Dedicated.
[06:30] Rebecca: That's a common path: start with PLG hosted for quick validation, then convert to Dedicated reserved capacity once you have predictable throughput. Dedicated setup involves capacity sizing and a short onboarding with engs, usually a 2-4 week ramp.
[06:50] Jorge: And private / on-prem — is there an air-gapped package?
[06:54] Carlos: Yes, we offer an on-prem package for regulated customers; it's a longer engagement (security assessments, network design, support SLA).

[07:20] Mark: Rate limits — for self-serve do you have per-API-key limits?
[07:24] Carlos: We enforce tiers and per-key quotas; for pilots we can loosen limits. Rate limiting is configurable per route in Dedicated.

[08:00] Aisha: For our pilot we'll need to replay ~1k rps bursts to validate autoscale. Does Redwood support burst capacity?
[08:09] Carlos: Dedicated supports burst policies and autoscaling; for hosted we have limits but can discuss elevated trial quotas for benchmark windows. We can run bench tests in your region or in our hosted environment with your sample workload.

[09:00] Rebecca: Quick question on success criteria — what would make this pilot a success in 4 weeks?
[09:07] Mark: For us: 1) produce latency reports meeting our SLOs, 2) cost per request < target (we'll share), and 3) prove data controls (audit logs, encryption).
[09:20] Aisha: And an internal sign-off path from security and procurement.

[10:00] Carlos: We'll need sample prompts and traffic patterns to run realistic benches. Can you share a small dataset + synthetic traffic?
[10:05] Mark: Yep we can. I'll package some anonymized prompts and a traffic profile.

[11:00] Jorge: One more thing — do you support tool-calling / function calls? We intend to have structured tool outputs.
[11:08] Carlos: Yes, Redwood supports function/tool calling and structured output; SDKs have helpers for streaming as well.

[12:00] Aisha: On compliance: does Redwood provide audit logs per API key and the ability to export logs to our SIEM?
[12:07] Carlos: Yes, for Dedicated and Private you can export audit logs to your log ingestion; hosted customers have export options and retention tiers as an add-on. I'll note that in the security pack.

[14:00] Rebecca: Great — next, I'll summarize pricing options. For hosted PLG it's usage-based with per-token rates and embedding units; Dedicated is a reserved capacity contract with committed monthly commit and lower unit cost; Private is enterprise licensing with platform fee. I'll share a short ROI calc.
[14:30] Mark: Do you have an estimate for conversion point where Dedicated becomes cheaper?
[14:35] Rebecca: We normally provide a breakeven chart — typically when sustained throughput exceeds X tokens/day (we'll calculate with your workload). I'll include a model-specific slide.

[16:00] Carlos: For the quickstart I'll walk you through the sample curl, Python SDK, and we'll provision a trial key. Example: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate — that's intentionally simple.
[16:25] Jorge: Good, minimal friction is key.

[18:00] Aisha: Any concerns on data residency? Some EU customers require all data stays in-region.
[18:06] Carlos: We support region constraints and can route to EU-hosted endpoints; for strict residency we recommend Private in-region or Dedicated in an EU region.

[19:00] Mark: For the trial, will we see per-token breakdown and cost analytics?
[19:06] Rebecca: Yes, Console shows token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and tracing hooks. We'll give you access to Console with the trial org.

[21:00] Aisha: Is there a SLA for hosted customers?
[21:06] Rebecca: Hosted has best-effort availability with standard support; Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets as an add-on.

[23:00] Jorge: Any gotchas around KV cache invalidation and multi-tenant prefix caching? We use caching on top of the model to shave cost.
[23:09] Carlos: Redwood has prefix/KV caching per org and deterministic cache keys; Dedicated gives you more control over cache policies. We'll share docs on cache eviction strategies.

[25:00] Mark: For our long-term plan, we may want hybrid: most traffic on Dedicated, a small set of high-compliance customers on Private. Does Redwood support routing policies?
[25:10] Carlos: Yes, smart routing lets you route by policy — latency, cost, or tenant. We can set fallbacks to hosted variants if capacity constrained.

[27:00] Aisha: Ok, let's talk logistics — timeline and stakeholders. Procurement will want the security docs and a contact for contracting.
[27:10] Rebecca: I'll include procurement contact details and our contracting team email in the follow-up. Also include standard terms and a dedicated onboarding lead for Dedicated or Private engagements.

[29:00] Mark: One last technical — do you support GPU-specific runtime flags, kernel selection or custom quantization?
[29:08] Carlos: On Dedicated and Private you can request specific runtime flags; the runtime picks optimized kernels based on model and sequence length; for Private we can expose more knobs. For hosted we apply safe defaults.

[31:00] Aisha: Great. Anything else from Redwood that helps us get started fast?
[31:05] Rebecca: We'll 1) provision the trial org with $500 credits, 2) share security pack link and SOC 2, 3) send a short dedicated vs hosted ROI slide, and 4) propose a benchmark slot for next week.

[33:00] Carlos: I'll include sample bench scripts (wrk + custom payloads) and a sample harness that replays your traffic. For the bench we can run a short burst test and a sustained throughput test.

[35:00] Jorge: Could you also include an example of the SDK call flow and how streaming increases throughput?
[35:06] Carlos: Yes — will include streaming examples and notes on KV cache and batching.

[37:00] Aisha: Ok that sounds good. We'll need to loop in security and procurement after we get your docs and the bench results.

[38:00] Rebecca: Quick recap of next steps — I'll send pricing & security docs, Carlos will provision trial credits and bench scripts, and Mark will share traffic patterns. We'll target the benchmark for 2026-03-10.
[38:18] Mark: Sounds good.
[38:25] Aisha: Thanks everyone — appreciate the clear next steps.

[40:00] Rebecca: Thanks all — we'll follow up by end of day with the links.
[40:06] Jorge: Thanks.
[40:12] Carlos: Thanks, bye.

Shared links mentioned: Security pack (link sent post-meeting), Pricing deck (link), Bench scripts (drive link), SDK quickstart (docs.redwood.ai/quickstart).

Notes on transcription quality: some overlaps and a few mis-heard words (proper nouns), but technical details and next steps captured.
